question: Is the remaining q7 transform-lattice distortion caused by sharing one scalar codebook across unequal axes, by fixed-FHT covariance-gauge mismatch, or by the scalar cell itself?

causal_parent.reason: The best compact scalar lattice has healthy occupancy but approximately twice the permitted distortion. Pure vector-cell shaping has an asymptotic gain ceiling below that factor, so source-axis and transform-gauge waste must be measured first.

arms.fht_global: fresh exact reproduction control for the rejected B32_q7 global scalar codebook
arms.fht_axis: same signed FHT and rate, but one 128-level scalar codebook per transform axis
arms.klt_global: probe-only covariance KLT with one global scalar codebook
arms.klt_axis: probe-only covariance KLT with axis-private scalar codebooks

theory.klt_definition: center source blocks, eigendecompose C = E[(y-mean)(y-mean)^T] = U Lambda U^T, and quantize (y-mean)U
theory.production_warning: The dense KLT requires about 64 dense MACs per weight for forward plus inverse transforms. It is an oracle ceiling only and cannot be selected as the production transform.

decision_tree.fht_axis_passes: Attribute the gap to axis heterogeneity. Implement axis-private levels with bit-packed q7 codes and require exact resume, MFU, and nine-update live direction gates.
decision_tree.only_klt_arm_passes: Attribute the gap to transform-gauge mismatch. Fit a fast learned butterfly to the measured KLT and require a frozen basis-approximation/recovery oracle before production implementation.
decision_tree.no_adapted_arm_passes: Close global and axis-private scalar transform cells at 7.25 bits/weight. Derive vector/trellis shaping with fractional-rate refinement; do not try more block sizes or integer-bit sweeps.
decision_tree.multiple_pass: Prefer fht_axis over any KLT arm because it preserves the fixed fast transform. KLT arms rank only the need for a learned transform.

execution_policy.preflight: foreground exact-config real-training preflight including all four attribution arms
execution_policy.scientific_run: foreground-polled because nine updates are expected under five minutes; attach a persistent @Codex watchdog immediately only if observed runtime exceeds five minutes
execution_policy.callbacks: none expected for a sub-five-minute diagnostic
